questions.content: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2.0 m/s² for 5.0 s. Find the distance travelled.
questions.markScheme: Correct SUVAT equation s = ut + ½at² (1); substitution u=0, a=2.0, t=5.0 (1); answer 25 m with units (1)
questions.understandingExplanation: When acceleration is constant and the initial speed is zero, the distance travelled in time t is s = ½at².
questions.scoringExplanation: Award method credit for selecting the correct SUVAT equation, then for correct substitution and units.

hints.title: Clarify
hints.content: List the given quantities: u = 0, a = 2.0 m/s², t = 5.0 s. You need the distance s.

hints.title: Knowledge
hints.content: This is constant-acceleration motion, so the SUVAT equations apply.

hints.title: Formula
hints.content: Which SUVAT equation links s, u, a and t without needing the final velocity v?

hints.title: Method
hints.content: Use s = ut + ½at² with u = 0, so s = ½at².

questions.understandingExplanation: micro (µ) represents a factor of 10⁻⁶; nano is 10⁻⁹, milli 10⁻³, mega 10⁶.
questions.scoringExplanation: One mark for correctly recalling the SI prefix meaning.

questions.content: Which of the following is the correct SI unit of momentum?
questions.correctDisplay: kg m s⁻¹ (equivalent to N s)
questions.understandingExplanation: Momentum p = mv has units kg × m s⁻¹ = kg m s⁻¹.
questions.scoringExplanation: One mark for selecting the correct SI unit of momentum.

questions.content: A body of mass 5 kg moves with velocity 4 m/s. Calculate its momentum, stating the units.
questions.correctDisplay: p = mv = 5 × 4 = 20 kg m s⁻¹ (N s)
questions.markScheme: p = mv (1); substitution 5 × 4 (1); answer 20 with units kg m s⁻¹ or N s (1)
questions.understandingExplanation: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity: p = mv.
questions.scoringExplanation: Three marks: formula, substitution, answer with correct units.

hints.title: Clarify
hints.content: List the given quantities: m = 5 kg, v = 4 m/s. You need momentum p.

hints.title: Knowledge
hints.content: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.

exerciseSets.title: Forces — resultant force with a diagram

questions.content: Two perpendicular forces act on a body: 3.0 N east and 4.0 N north. Find the magnitude of the resultant force.
questions.imageDescription: A right triangle showing a 3.0 N force pointing east along the base and a 4.0 N force pointing north along the height, with the resultant as the hypotenuse.

markScheme.criterion: Recognise the two forces are perpendicular

questions.understandingExplanation: For perpendicular forces the resultant magnitude is found by Pythagoras.

hints.title: Clarify
hints.content: The two forces are at right angles. Sketch them as two sides of a right triangle.

hints.title: Knowledge
hints.content: Perpendicular forces combine via Pythagoras, not simple addition.
